messages:
elaine: Working on the PRD for docs-as-spec quickstarts. Draft here: https://redwood.internal/docs/prd/docs-as-spec-quickstart (WIP). Need acceptance criteria + edge cases so these can double as CI smoke tests. TL;DR: quickstart = 5-min tutorial + runnable example + small test harness that validates core API surface.

sam: Got it, will review. Two quick questions up front: what does "passing" look like in CI, and how strict are perf SLOs for the quickstart tests? Also we should decide which SDKs are required for GA.

maria: From eng perspective, propose concrete acceptance criteria: 1) Example app boots locally with docker-compose in <2 minutes on dev laptop, 2) CI job runs a smoke test asserting 3 core flows (generate, stream, embed) succeed, 3) No prod credentials required (use mock or sandbox keys). Edge cases to call out: model mismatch (model name/version), intermittent network failures, rate-limited responses. I'll sketch a minimal test harness.

pranav: For devex: require code samples in JS + Python + curl, minimal fixture dataset, and a single-config quickstart (env file) so users don't manage multiple secrets. Suggest we add a check-list section in the docs that maps each bullet to a CI job name so we can auto-validate.

jordan: Design needs: 2 static screenshots (getting started & result), 1 short gif showing streaming output, and standardized error-state copy for common failures (timeout, auth error, model not found). Keep visual assets tiny.

elaine: I've added a minimal spec in the PRD under "Acceptance Criteria (quickstarts)". Copying the draft smoke commands here for feedback: 

```
# local quickstart smoke (example)
docker compose up --build -d
./scripts/wait-for-service.sh localhost:8080
curl -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"prompt":"echo-token-count"}' http://localhost:8080/generate
```

Are these sufficient for a CI smoke test or do we need more deterministic assertions? :eyes:

maria: Few tweaks: 1) include the header in the curl example (you did), 2) make the test assert a deterministic token/phrase: if prompt is "echo-token-count", expect response contains "echo-token-count" so CI isn't flaky. Example assertion: `status == 200 && body.choices[0].text.includes('echo-token-count')`. Also add a mocked-model mode for CI to avoid external infra flakiness.

sam: @maria can you add that assertion to the CI template? Also propose perf SLOs: cold-start < 1.5s, p95 < 250ms for 32-token responses on the hosted dev tier. We can relax post-GA for extended examples.

pranav: Perf SLOs LGTM. For CI robustness: if quickstart references hosted API, use a recorded fixture or a local mock server. Add an env var RUN_QUICKSTART_TESTS=true so test matrix can skip on forks. We'll need small README snippet explaining how to run locally vs CI.

jordan: I'll create placeholder assets and add alt text for accessibility. Quick question: do we require streaming in the GA quickstart or can streaming be an extended example?

elaine: Good point. My vote is GA = non-streaming minimal path + explicit note/link to streaming quickstart (post-GA). That cuts scope. @sam please confirm.

sam: Agree — GA minimal scope: one model, one SDK (JS), non-streaming quickstart + curl. Streaming and Python + extended examples post-GA. Timeline: 2 weeks to get PRD finalized, 1 week dev spike, then docs. Marking as priority on roadmap.

ci-bot: CI job created: docs/quickstart-smoke (manual trigger).

elaine: Thanks all — I'll update the PRD with the CI assertion and GA scope notes. Will ping again when draft PR is ready for final sign-off. :thumbsup:
